html:
The Siriano, or Siria-masã, are an Eastern Tucanoan people of the Vaupés region on the border of Colombia and Brazil, living along the Paca and Viña rivers. They speak one of the Tucanoan languages.

Like the Tuyuka and other peoples of the Vaupés, they marry outside their own language group, so families mix several languages. Their villages were centred on large communal longhouses called malocas. Catholic missions and rubber collecting reached the region in the 1900s. Only a few hundred Siriano live today.
